title: Conversation velocity allocation notebook
content:
Purpose and framing:
This is a quick-running scratchpad to explore a different axis for packaging: conversation velocity (messages/min or tokens/min) rather than pure tokens or session counts. In many interactive UIs the dominant driver of cost is the rate at which the client issues requests (concurrency + frequency) and the backend's ability to amortize KV-cache + batching. We want a compact set of tier concepts that align incentives: predictable unit economics for Redwood, understandable knobs for product teams, and simple UX for customers.

Key definitions (working):
- Conversation velocity (CV): average tokens generated per minute per active user (tpm). Optionally measured as messages/minute * avg tokens per response.
- Active window: 30s-2m sliding window used to detect bursts.
- Tranche: an allocation bucket in a plan that gives a per-minute entitlement (e.g., 120 tpm) plus a baseline token pool.
- Pulse/Cadence/Tide: tier names used in scenarios below (keep human-friendly).

Assumptions for back-of-envelope math (adjustable):
- GPU-hour cost allocated to tokens: 0.18 USD / GPU-hour => approx 2M tokens per GPU-hour (quantized/optimized). So base cost per 1k tokens = 0.00009 USD. Use rounded 0.0001 USD / 1k tokens for conservative margins.
- KV cache hit: 30% token reduction on average for repeat prompts (conservative).
- Batching efficiency: for steady-state high CV, effective per-token cost improves by 20% (fewer context swaps, higher utilization).
- Non-token overhead (routing, request, IO): ~0.00002 USD per request on average (small but matters for high-frequency microcalls).
- Customer-facing rounding and margins: aim for 3x markup on pure infra cost for hosted payg unit price (covers infra, support, and margins).

Simple formulas (BOE):
- infra_cost_per_1k_tokens = 0.0001 USD (after rounding)
- retail_price_per_1k_tokens = infra_cost_per_1k_tokens * 3 = 0.0003 USD
- effective_tokens_consumed = raw_tokens * (1 - cache_hit_rate)
- per-request-surcharge = 0.00002 USD * request_count

Design sketch: Tranche-backed minutes
Idea: Each plan allocates: a baseline monthly token pool (pool_tokens) + a per-minute tranche (tpm) that grants elevated throughput for interactive windows. Tranches reset each minute (or use rolling window) and allow smoothing of spikes without forcing customers to buy extreme monthly pool.

Example: Pulse (Starter)
- Price: $20 / mo
- Baseline pool: 200k tokens / mo
- Tranche: 60 tpm for up to 6 concurrent sessions (i.e., short interactive apps)
- Overages: retail_price_per_1k_tokens beyond pool, or throttled after 3x tranche sustained for 1 minute
- BOE: If customer uses steady 60 tpm for 30 minutes/day: 60 tpm * 30 min * 30 days = 54k tokens/month consumed from tranche/pool. Remaining headroom covers typical variance.

Cadence (SMB)
- Price: $250 / mo
- Baseline pool: 3M tokens / mo
- Tranche: 600 tpm across tenant, supports 50 concurrent micro-sessions
- Soft-guarantee: up to 3x tranche for short bursts (throttle/fallback beyond)
- BOE: 3M tokens @ infra cost => 3M/1k * 0.0001 = $0.30 infra cost, retail revenue ~ $0.90 => obvious heavy margins to cover support/Ops. Need to think about fairness for highly bursty customers.

Tide (Enterprise starter)
- Price: custom / $2k+ mo
- Baseline pool: 30M tokens
- Tranche: 6k tpm, SLA-backed latency/throughput tiers and can request dedicated capacity

Burst credit mechanics (sketch):
- Maintain two counters: monthly_pool_remaining, rolling_minute_tranche_remaining. A request consumes from tranche first (if within rolling window) then monthly pool, then overage pricing.
- To preserve SLOs we can allow temporary overage draw up to X% of tranche (credit line) with billing reconciliation (invoiced).

Why CV helps (hypotheses):
- Aligns price with resource contention: lots of small, frequent calls force more context switches and hurt throughput; CV directly correlates with that.
- Easier to reason about for product teams building chatty features (rate budgets map to cost).
- Gives us levers to offer better unit economics for customers who can restructure UX (longer replies, fewer pings) — aligns incentives to optimize prompts.

Potential anti-abuse / edge cases:
- Bots opening many long-polling sessions to consume tranche: limit tranche to N concurrent sessions per API key, charge per concurrent session beyond threshold.
- Unbounded message size: cap per-message tokens or meter raw input+output tokens equally.
- Gamey pacing: customers could alternate many micro-sessions to flatten per-minute counts; impose a minimal per-session activity floor for tranche eligibility.

Worked example (detailed):
Customer: micro-co building in-chat suggestions. Typical session: 5 messages request-response, avg 80 output tokens, 10 input tokens => 450 tokens / session. 6 sessions active per minute on average => CV = 6 * 450 = 2700 tpm.
- If they pick Cadence (600 tpm tranche + 3M pool): immediate overage of 2100 tpm during active periods. Over a month of 10k active minutes: incremental tokens = 2100 * 10k = 21M tokens extra. Retail overage revenue = 21M/1k * 0.0003 = $6.3k. Infra cost = 21M/1k * 0.0001 = $2.1k. Gross on that usage ~ $4.2k.
- Observation: Tranche sizing must reflect typical CV for target segment; otherwise customers quickly move to overage.

Open parameters and experiments to run:
- Measure real CV distribution across 30 pilot customers for 4 weeks. Capture median, 90p, and burst percentiles in tpm and concurrent sessions.
- A/B test two calculations: tranche-size = median CV * safety_factor (1.5) vs tranche-size = 75p CV. See retention and overage churn.
- Simulate amortized infra using measured cache hit and batching uplift per CV bucket; feed into price recommendation engine.

UX implications (billing page / console):
- Show live CV meter (tpm, concurrent sessions) and projected monthly burn at current rate.
- Visualize tranche consumption (live and predicted) and a one-click upgrade path to next tranche.
- Explain how caching and prompt design reduce CV cost (practical tips).

Next steps (actionable):
- Instrument telemetry event: tokens_out_per_min_per_key, active_sessions_per_min_per_key. Aggregate for cohort analysis. (JIRA: JIRA-PR-2931)
- Spin up a 4-week pilot with 20 SMB customers on Cadence-style tranches and track overage/reallocation patterns.
- Build quick pricing simulator (spreadsheet or tiny web tool) that lets sales/solutions input sample CV and outputs recommended plan and expected monthly bill.

Unresolved questions / notes to self:
- How to incorporate embeddings / batch-only workloads into CV model (different resource profile). Might need a separate tranche logic or exclude embeddings from per-minute entitlements.
- How to translate dedicated capacity discounts into tranche equivalents. Some enterprise customers will prefer seat-like guarantees rather than token tranches.
- Consider a lightweight session-affinity metric to improve KV cache hit and then let customers purchase 'cache affinity' as a premium feature.

This doc is rough — use it as a seed for experiments and a source of prompts for the pricing workshop next Tuesday.

Quick checklist for pilot:
- [ ] Add metrics to infra (tokens/min by key)
- [ ] Build simulator spreadsheet (tab: tranche sizing)
- [ ] Recruit 15–25 pilot customers (growth + sales)
- [ ] Draft email + console messaging for trial

End of scratchpad.
